clue.text: Lay aside temporarily book in college building after test

indicators.note: after places the test's letters at the front, the college building following them

parts.note: MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles

indicators.note: in puts the book's abbreviation inside the college building

parts.note: a hall is a college building, such as a hall of residence

explanation.surface: Someone shelves a plan for a new college building until a test is passed.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness test for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in storage, as clothes once were among camphor, is to shelve it for later use.

clue.text: Demand made by police

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Demand made by police (6)' for MARKET: MET (police) round ARK would work, but no clue word gives ARK as held; 'made' looks misread or a word is missing.

clue.text: Resort not set for renovation

indicators.note: for renovation suggests the letters of not set are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday town is being refurbished but isn't ready yet.
explanation.walkthrough: Totnes is a market town in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Devon visited by tourists, so a holiday destination.

clue.text: Flourishing sign shown by Luxembourg in prosperity

indicators.note: in places the country's code within the word for prosperity

parts.note: a boom is a period of prosperity
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: Luxembourg shows signs of thriving during an economic upturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourishing' works as a noun here: being in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of health and vigour, like a flower at its peak.

clue.text: Latin work proving profitable for student

parts.note: an earner is something, such as a job, that brings in money

explanation.surface: A student finds that studying Latin pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being taught, a pupil or trainee.

clue.text: Shares held back company supplying decorative work

indicators.note: held back tells us the word for shares is written from right to left

parts.note: cuts are shares, as in a cut of the profits

explanation.surface: A firm that makes ornamental plasterwork is holding back its dividend.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental plaster applied to walls and ceilings is a classic form of decorative finish.

clue.text: Flying rota we set for small plane

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters of rota we set are tossed about

explanation.surface: A pilot sets out a rota for flying a light aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A light aircraft with room for only a pilot and one passenger.

clue.text: Loss of nerve shown by Arctic walkers?

definitions.meaning: a sudden fear that makes someone back out
the chilly limbs of anyone walking in the polar north

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for losing courage before an event, and literally the chilled extremities of polar hikers.

clue.text: Shrub growing little when bordered by European flower

indicators.note: when bordered by puts the river's letters on either side of the thin word

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Oder is a European river
lean means thin, growing little in bulk

explanation.surface: A shrub grows poorly when surrounded by European blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river here, not a bloom: the Oder runs along the German–Polish border.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen Mediterranean bush with pink or white blossom.

clue.text: Sensible illustration a lecturer included

indicators.note: included signals that the letters sit within the run of words illustration a lecturer

explanation.surface: A lecturer adds a sensible picture to the talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reasonable and logical is to be level-headed, guided by reason.

clue.text: Man in the pits not right for dog

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for right from the miner's word

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner, a man who works in the pits

explanation.surface: A miner who isn't right turns out to be a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish sheepdog breed, so an example of a dog.

clue.text: Sound of exhaust — feature of car?

indicators.note: sound of says the word for exhaust is heard, not seen

parts.note: to exhaust is to tire

explanation.surface: Someone hears the exhaust and wonders whether it is part of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber wheel covering, part of every motor vehicle.

clue.text: Iron linked with brass? Very likely!

parts.note: to iron is to smooth or even out
brass is slang for money

explanation.surface: Is iron really going to be combined with brass? Highly probable, says someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is ironic: odds of evens mean a fifty-fifty chance, which is only middling likely.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds of evens describe an outcome as probable as not, here given a sardonic tone.

clue.text: Mischievous fellow encompassed by fanciful line

indicators.note: encompassed by puts the fellow's abbreviation inside the reworked line
fanciful suggests the word line is rearranged imaginatively

explanation.surface: A naughty chap is caught up in an imaginative line of talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fanciful' rearranges LINE as ELIN, and 'encompassed by' places F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish and puckish, like a sprite of folklore.

clue.text: Pleasing do for audience

indicators.note: for audience says the word for do is heard rather than read

parts.note: to do well or badly is to fare

explanation.surface: An agreeable party is put on for the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive or pleasant to look at, as in a lady of beauty.

clue.text: Animal, one turning course with small measure

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

indicators.note: turning says the course and the small measure are both read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a course of duties taken in turn
a gill is a small liquid measure

explanation.surface: An animal is turning in its course with a small measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses ROTA plus GILL to give LLIGATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A large reptile of the crocodile family, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Last former partner very good? Not half!

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: Not half says only part of the word for very good survives, its second half dropped

parts.note: tremendous means very good

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the final ex was very good and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' sounds like British slang for 'definitely', but it means cutting TREMENDOUS to TREME.
explanation.definitionFit: Outermost or furthest, at the very end of something.

clue.text: Salesman with skill starts to exemplify enterprising ability in exchange

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
art means skill

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of exemplify and enterprising

explanation.surface: A salesman shows off his skill in trade negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick wit in conversation, a talent for clever retorts.

clue.text: Singular weapon commanding attention

parts.note: a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: A single weapon makes people take notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and harsh, demanding to be heard.

clue.text: Girl making exotic tea sell

indicators.note: exotic suggests the letters of tea and sell are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: A girl earns a living selling unusual teas.
explanation.walkthrough: Estella is the heroine of Dickens's Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Tell, maybe, without hesitation there's a vaulted entrance

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the hesitation sound from the bowman's word

parts.note: William Tell is the most famous archer of legend
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: A story-teller speaks without pausing about an arched doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb, but it is William Tell, the Swiss archer.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved structure spanning a doorway or passage.

clue.text: Annoy copper

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for to irritate, and also for an informer working for the police.

clue.text: Present past indication of disapproval

parts.note: now is the present time
then refers to a past time

explanation.surface: Someone tuts disapprovingly about past and present.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation used to rebuke or caution, a spoken reproof.

clue.text: Almost unseemly street abroad around one square

indicators.note: around puts the French street around the other pieces

parts.note: rue is French for street
I is the Roman numeral for one
SQ is the abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: A foreign street around a square is nearly indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly indecent, bordering on the improper.

clue.text: Do not accept flawed article

definitions.meaning: an item discarded because it is faulty

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means turn down; as a noun it is a substandard item set aside.

clue.text: Getting on nag in gymkhana without trappings

indicators.note: without trappings means the outer letters of the run nag in gymkhana are stripped away

explanation.surface: An old horse is still competing at the gymkhana without its harness.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymkhana is a horse-riding competition, often for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older, idiomatically described as getting on in years.

clue.text: Chickens' quality is lower I read when placed around entrance to coop

parts.note: to lower can mean to cow, to look threatening and intimidate

indicators.note: around puts the reworked letters on either side of the coop's first letter
placed signals that the letters of I read are set out in a new order
entrance to picks out the opening letter of coop

explanation.surface: A farmer reads about the timid nature of hens near the henhouse door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed' rearranges I READ as ARDIE, and 'around' wraps it round C from 'entrance to coop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a chicken means a coward, so this is a lack of courage.

clue.text: Part of flight heading north from Azores I relish

indicators.note: heading north says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: On a flight heading north from the Azores, someone enjoys the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'heading north' reads the letters upwards; 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not an air journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical piece of each stair in a staircase.

clue.text: Negotiation about a ton within the borders of Turkey

indicators.note: within puts the inner pieces between the outside letters of Turkey
the borders of picks the first and last letters of Turkey

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Talks on the Turkish border cover about a ton of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal agreement between states, the product of diplomatic talks.

clue.text: Build feeling of anger about shy agitation

indicators.note: about places the angry feeling around the rearranged letters

parts.note: pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment

indicators.note: agitation suggests the letters of shy are stirred up

explanation.surface: A shy person's nervousness turns to anger over their body shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitation' turns SHY into HYS, which 'about' places inside PIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bodily form or frame is their build.

clue.text: Restaurant that's English and tasteless giving up opening

indicators.note: giving up opening says the first letter of the word for tasteless is dropped

parts.note: watery food is bland and tasteless

explanation.surface: An English diner serves bland food and has closed its doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual place to dine, a café or diner.

clue.text: Unusually great sin getting cross above all others

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters of great sin come in an odd order

explanation.surface: Committing an especially serious sin makes someone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross means irate, and the superlative form means most irate of all.
